question: If sin (p + q) = 1 and cos (p - q) = (sqrt3)/(2), find p
solution:
**Given:**

 sin (p + q) = 1

cos (p - q) = (sqrt3)/(2)

**Concept used:**

Sin90°= 1, cos**3**0° =(sqrt3)/(2) ** **

**Calculation:**

 sin (p + q) = 1

⇒ sin (p + q) = sin 90° 

⇒ p+q = 90°

Again,

cos (p - q) = (sqrt3)/(2)

⇒ cos (p - q) = cos 30° 

⇒ (p - q) = 30° 

p = 1/2 (p+q + p - q)

⇒ 1/2 (90+30) = 60°
